LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.codeRate: For positive blocklength n and message count M ≥ 1, the rate is (ln M)/n nats per use. The total definition gives zero if the blocklength or message count is zero.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.codeRate_nonneg: For M ≥ 1, a code with n uses and M messages has nonnegative rate.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.codeRate_zero: For any message count M, the rate assigned to a code of blocklength zero is zero.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.codeRate_one: A code with one message has rate zero at every blocklength.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.codeRate_le_iff: For n > 0 and M ≥ 1, the rate is at most R exactly when M ≤ exp(nR).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.exp_mul_codeRate: For n > 0 and M ≥ 1, if r is the rate (ln M)/n, then exp(nr) = M.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.roundedMessageSiz: The rounded message count at blocklength n and real target rate R is the smallest natural number at least exp(nR).
For any n and real R, the rounded count M = ⌈exp(nR)⌉ is at least one and satisfies exp(nR) ≤ M < exp(nR) + 1.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.codeRate_roundedM: For n > 0 and target R ≥ 0, using M = ⌈exp(nR)⌉ gives rate r satisfying R ≤ r ≤ R + (ln 2)/n.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.ceil_natsToBits_l: For M ≥ 1 and any nonnegative integer k, ⌈log₂ M⌉ ≤ k if and only if M ≤ 2ᵏ.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.natsToBits_codeRa: A code with 2ᵏ messages has rate k/n bits per use. At n = 0 the common value is defined to be zero.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.codeRate_sub_log_: If n > 0, M ≥ 1 and M ≤ 2L, the rate at L messages is at least the rate at M messages minus (ln 2)/n. Equivalently, (ln L)/n ≥ (ln M)/n − (ln 2)/n.
